title_eng: Effect of Low Sampling Rate on the First Derivative of the PPG Waveform
title_kor: Effect of Low Sampling Rate on the First Derivative of the PPG Waveform
abstract:
Abstract—The purpose of this paper is to investigate how the 
PPG derivative waveform is changed at low sampling rates. For 
this purpose, PPG derivatives, obtained at 10 kHz sampling 
frequency(fs) and the down-sampled PPGs at 5 kHz, 1 kHz, 500 
Hz, 100 Hz, 50 Hz, 25 Hz and 10 Hz, were compared. In order to 
quantitatively evaluate the variation according to the sampling 
rate, we used the Lorentz plot and the changes of SD1 and SD2 
were observed. As a result, in the PPG, SDs varied at fs ≤ 25 Hz, 
but in the case of the PPG derivative, SDs change rapidly at fs ≤ 
100 Hz. When the BPF was applied to the PPG before 
differentiation, the deviation was larger at fs ≤ 25 Hz as in the 
case of the PPG. This suggests that the BPF should be preceded 
for use the PPG derivative sampled at low frequencies. 
I. INTRODUCTION 
PPG (Photoplethysmography) is a non-invasive technique 
that observes blood volume changes in vessels or tissues 
beneath the skin. Selecting the appropriate sampling frequency 
for optimal PPG measurement has been an important topic, 
and recently a pilot study suggested 25 Hz as a minimal 
sampling frequency to prevent aliasing [1]. However, studies 
on the effect of sampling frequency on PPG derivatives are 
still insufficient in spite of the PPG derivative is a promising 
indicator in analyzing vascular characteristic as well as in 
finding feature points of PPG waveform [2, 3]. In this study, 
we investigated the variation of PPG derivative waveforms at 
low sampling rates for advanced PPG derivative studies

I. INTRODUCTION 
PPG (Photoplethysmography) is a non-invasive technique 
that observes blood volume changes in vessels or tissues 
beneath the skin. Selecting the appropriate sampling frequency 
for optimal PPG measurement has been an important topic, 
and recently a pilot study suggested 25 Hz as a minimal 
sampling frequency to prevent aliasing [1]. However, studies 
on the effect of sampling frequency on PPG derivatives are 
still insufficient in spite of the PPG derivative is a promising 
indicator in analyzing vascular characteristic as well as in 
finding feature points of PPG waveform [2, 3]. In this study, 
we investigated the variation of PPG derivative waveforms at 
low sampling rates for advanced PPG derivative studies 
II. MATERIALS AND METHODS 
We obtained PPG from 10 volunteer (4 females, 21±1.5 
years old, 169.3±7.1 cm, 65.5±11.2 kg) by using MP150, 
OXY100E (Biopac Systems, Inc., CA, USA) in the supine 
position during rest. Signal was recorded with 20-minute 
length, and sampling frequency(fs) was 10 kHz. PPG was 
down-sampled by decimation as to 5 kHz, 1 kHz, 500 Hz, 100 
Hz, 50 Hz, 25 Hz and 10 Hz, respectively, and differentiated. 
In order to quantitatively evaluation of the waveform change, 
the deviation in the inverse proportional direction (SD1) and 
the deviation in the proportional direction (SD2) on the Lorenz 
plot of the down-sampled PPG and the 10 kHz PPG are 
calculated according to the fs. 
III. RESULT AND DISCUSSION 
Table 1 shows the changes of deviation rate, and Fig. 1(a), 
(b) and (c) show the Lorenz plot of a 10 kHz PPG and down-
sampled PPGs, PPG derivative of 10 kHz PPG and down-
sampled PPG without BPF (band pass filtering), and PPG 
derivative of 10 kHz PPG and down-sampled PPG after BPF, 
respectively. In Fig. 1(a), because the most power of PPG is 
concentrated under around 10 Hz, we found that the aliasing 
begins at fs ≤ 25Hz. This high frequency distortion drastically 
increased the SD1. However, the SD2 was decreased because 
extremes cannot be detected exactly. In Fig. 1(b), very high 
SD1 and SD2 were observed, and it was speculated that 
derivative waveform was severely distorted by differentiation 
because the most power of PPG is concentrated on low 
frequency range but differentiation works like high pass filter 
(HPF) that could reduce the frequency power of PPG 
waveform range. This speculation is proved in Fig. 1(c). 
Applying BPF which has 0.5 to 10 Hz passband before 
differentiation reduce deviations successfully, and it shows 
similar results with not-differentiated PPG. 
IV. CONCLUSION 
We investigated the sampling frequency effect on the PPG 
derivative waveform. Differentiation could reduce signal-to-
noise ratio of PPG due to the HPF-like effect, thus BPF or LPF 
are recommended before differentiation. We will also examine 
the effect of second derivative in our future study. 
REFERENCES

assessment of how low can we go to analyze pulse rate variability with 
reliability?," Physiological Measurement, vol. 38, no. 3, p. 586, 2017. 
[2] M. Elgendi, "On the analysis of fingertip photoplethysmogram signals," 
Curr Cardiol Rev, vol. 8, no. 1, pp. 14-25, Feb 2012. 
[3] K. Takazawa et al., "Assessment of vasoactive agents and vascular aging 
by the second derivative of photoplethysmogram waveform," 
Hypertension, vol. 32, no. 2, pp. 365-70, Aug 1998.
